before.title: Headlight Assembly Moisture Intrusion / Condensation
before.description: Palisade headlight assemblies are prone to moisture intrusion and internal condensation, significantly reducing nighttime visibility. The issue stems from inadequate sealing of the LED headlight housing. Some owners have had multiple headlight replacements under warranty, only for the issue to return.
before.solution: Document the condensation with photos and bring to dealer under warranty. Hyundai has updated headlight assemblies with improved sealing (newer part numbers). If out of warranty, a headlight assembly replacement is $800-1,500 per side. Some owners have had success drilling a tiny drain hole and applying silicone sealant as a temporary fix.
symptoms: Visible condensation inside headlight
Reduced headlight brightness
Water droplets visible inside lens
Headlight flickers
One headlight appears dimmer than the other

before.title: ABS / Traction Control Malfunction on Rough Roads (Class-Action Braking Defect)
before.description: On 2023-2025 Palisades, the ABS and traction control systems can miscalculate wheel speeds when braking on gravel, dirt, or uneven surfaces, triggering rapid release-and-reapply cycling that lengthens stopping distances and, in some reports, spikes steering effort. A class-action complaint (Maldonado v. Hyundai Motor America) was filed May 9, 2025 in the Central District of California alleging the defect across 2023-2025 model years.
before.solution: No recall has been issued and NHTSA had not opened a formal investigation as of mid-2026; the matter is the subject of an active class-action lawsuit. Affected owners should file a complaint at nhtsa.gov, document incidents, and have the dealer check for ABS/ESC software updates. Increase following distance on loose or rough surfaces until a remedy is available.
symptoms: ABS pulses or engages on gravel/dirt/rough roads with little braking
Greatly increased stopping distance over uneven surfaces
Steering feels locked/heavy during the event
Traction control activates erratically on bumps

before.title: Foul Cabin Odor from Headrests / Interior Materials
before.description: Many Palisade owners report a persistent foul odor inside the cabin, described as a chemical or locker-room smell. The source has been traced to the Nappa leather headrests and interior trim materials off-gassing. The smell is worse in warm weather and returns even after cleaning. This was a widespread complaint in early production models.
before.solution: Hyundai issued a customer satisfaction campaign replacing headrests in affected vehicles. Contact your dealer to check eligibility. For DIY treatment, clean headrests with a leather cleaner and apply Leather Honey conditioner. Using an ozone generator ($30-50 rental) can temporarily eliminate the odor. Dealer headrest replacement is free if covered.
symptoms: Chemical or musty smell in cabin
Odor worse in warm weather
Smell returns after cleaning
Headrests smell when held close
New car smell that turns unpleasant

communityRecommendations.content: Leather Honey leather conditioner works well to reduce the off-gassing odor after deep cleaning

proposal.title: Foul Cabin Odor from Headrests / Interior Materials
proposal.description: Hyundai TSB 21-BD-002H-1 applies to certain model-year 2020-2021 Palisade (LX2) vehicles equipped with Nappa leather and produced before November 23, 2020. The bulletin documents odor that may emit from one or more headrests.
proposal.solution: Ask a Hyundai dealer to inspect the headrests under TSB 21-BD-002H-1. Hyundai's procedure removes the affected headrests, applies an approved odor eliminator to the foam, inner cover surfaces and seat mounting holes, dries the treatment in direct sunlight for two to three hours and reinspects. Only a headrest that still has odor after treatment is replaced.
symptoms: Odor emitting from one or more headrests

before.title: Idle Stop & Go (ISG) Electric Oil Pump Controller Fire Risk — Recall 246 / 23V526
before.description: The electronic controller for the Idle Stop & Go transmission electric oil pump on 2023-2024 Palisades may have a printed circuit board damaged during manufacturing (e.g., a damaged capacitor) that can overheat the pump circuit board, connector, and wiring harness, raising the risk of an engine-compartment fire whether parked or driving. A separate 2025-model-year recall covers an insufficient controller seal that lets moisture reach the PCB. Hyundai advises owners to park outside away from structures until repaired.
before.solution: Recall #246 / NHTSA 23V526 (2023-2024 Palisade plus 2023 Tucson, Sonata, Elantra, Kona): dealers inspect and replace the ISG electric oil pump controller as necessary, free of charge; owner letters mailed from September 7, 2023. The 2025-model seal/moisture issue is addressed under a separate recall (NHTSA 25V291). Park outside until repaired; Hyundai customer service 1-855-371-9460.
symptoms: Burning smell or smoke from engine compartment
Warning to park outside / fire-risk recall notice
Possible ISG / auto stop-start malfunction warning

The transmission electric oil pump for the Idle Stop & Go system may contain a controller printed circuit board damaged during manufacturing. A damaged capacitor can cause heat damage to the pump circuit board, connector and wiring harness, increasing fire risk and potentially disrupting communication among onboard controllers.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for NHTSA recall 23V-526. Hyundai recommends parking affected vehicles outside and away from structures until the recall remedy is completed. Hyundai dealers inspect and replace the electric oil pump and front harness as necessary, free of charge.
symptoms: Smoke from the vehicle underbody
Burning or melting odor
Malfunction Indicator Lamp or other dashboard warning lamps

before.title: Infotainment Screen Blackout & BlueLink Telematics Failures
before.description: Palisade owners report the central infotainment/navigation screen going black and unresponsive, taking out GPS, Bluetooth audio, and the backup camera at once, sometimes requiring a costly head-unit replacement. Separately, BlueLink remote start and app functions stop working, often after software updates, forcing use of the physical key. These are recurring software/head-unit and telematics faults documented across owner forums rather than a single recall.
before.solution: Reset the head unit by holding the small pinhole reset next to the tuner knob (~15 seconds with a paperclip), or hold Map + Setup ~10 seconds. Install the latest infotainment software (USB or OTA) and update the BlueLink app; reactivate BlueLink in Setup (support 1-844-258-5656). Persistent blackouts may require head-unit reflash or replacement under warranty.
symptoms: Center screen black/unresponsive (no GPS, Bluetooth, or backup camera)
BlueLink remote start/app fails after an update
BlueLink shows signal bars but a red 'no service' indicator
Wireless CarPlay / Wi-Fi will not connect

before.title: Oil Dilution / Gasoline Contamination in Engine Oil
before.description: The 3.8L Lambda II V6 in the Palisade can suffer from fuel diluting the engine oil, particularly in cold climates with short trips. The GDI system can allow unburned fuel past the piston rings during cold starts. Oil level rises above the full mark and smells of gasoline. Hyundai released a software update to address the issue.
before.solution: Have the dealer install the latest ECU calibration to reduce fuel enrichment during cold starts. Change oil more frequently in winter (every 3,000-5,000 miles vs 7,500). Use 0W-20 full synthetic oil. If oil level is significantly above the full mark, drain and replace immediately. Software update is free; extra oil changes cost $50-80 each.
symptoms: Oil level rising above full mark
Gasoline smell from dipstick
Oil looks thin and watery
Rough idle in cold weather
Fuel smell inside cabin

citations.title: Hyundai TSB 20-FL-006 - Oil Dilution Cold Climate
PalisadeForum.com - Oil Dilution Reports

communityRecommendations.content: Pennzoil Platinum 0W-20 resists fuel dilution better than many conventional oils
In cold weather, drive at least 15-20 minutes to get the engine fully warmed up - short trips cause the most dilution
Check oil level and smell the dipstick monthly in winter months to catch dilution early

before.title: Seat Belt Buckle Fails to Latch (Out-of-Spec Buckle Assembly) — Recall 25V607
before.description: On 2020-2025 Palisades, out-of-spec components in the front and second-row outboard seat belt buckles increase friction in the latch channel (worse in cold weather), so the tongue plate may not fully latch. NHTSA opened a probe in August 2024 after 37 unbuckling complaints, leading to recall 25V-607 covering 568,580 vehicles. An unlatched belt will not restrain an occupant in a crash.
before.solution: Recall 25V-607 (Hyundai #283): dealers inspect the front and second-row outboard seat belt buckles and replace any defective assemblies free of charge. Until repaired, insert the belt firmly with a quick, direct motion and tug to confirm it is latched. Verify your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.
symptoms: Seat belt clicks but pops open / will not stay latched
Harder to latch in cold temperatures
Tongue plate inserts but does not catch
Belt warning chime stays on with belt apparently buckled

proposal.title: Seat Belt Buckle Fails to Latch (Out-of-Spec Buckle Assembly) — Recall 25V607
proposal.description: NHTSA recall 25V-607 (Hyundai recall 283) covers certain model-year 2020-2025 Palisades. Front-row and second-row outer seat-belt buckle assemblies may contain out-of-specification components that interfere within the latch channel and increase friction, especially in cold temperatures. Together with slow insertion of the tongue plate, this may prevent the buckle from fully latching and increase injury risk in a crash.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for NHTSA recall 25V-607. Until the repair is completed, Hyundai advises fastening the belt with a quick and direct motion, then pulling on it to confirm it is fully secured. Hyundai dealers replace the applicable front-row and second-row outer buckle assemblies free of charge.
symptoms: Lighter-than-normal audible click while fastening
Recessed push button on the buckle housing
Visual or audible seat-belt warning if the belt is not secured

before.title: Third-Row Side Curtain Airbag Improper Deployment (FMVSS 226 Failure) — Recall 26V034
before.description: Certain 2020-2025 Palisades built April 10, 2019 through June 16, 2025 do not meet Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 226 (ejection mitigation). NHTSA compliance testing on a 2025 Palisade measured third-row occupant head movement beyond the 100 mm limit, meaning the third-row side curtain airbags may deploy improperly and fail to protect occupants in a crash or rollover. Recall 26V034 (Hyundai #292) covers 568,576 vehicles.
before.solution: Recall 26V034 (Hyundai #292): dealers install a protective film over the rear window and remove interior padding as necessary, free of charge. Interim notification letters were mailed beginning March 13, 2026; the final remedy was anticipated around May 2026. Verify your VIN with a Hyundai dealer or at nhtsa.gov/recalls.
symptoms: No driver-noticeable symptom (latent crash-safety defect)
Affects third-row occupant protection in side impacts and rollovers

before.title: 8-Speed Automatic Harsh Shifting / Delayed Downshift
before.description: The 8-speed automatic transmission in the Palisade can exhibit harsh 1-2 and 2-3 upshifts, delayed downshifts when passing, and occasional harsh engagement from park to drive. The TCM calibration is the primary issue, though some cases involve valve body wear. Hyundai has released multiple software updates to improve shift quality.
before.solution: Request the latest TCM software update from the dealer (free under warranty). Ensure transmission fluid is at the correct level and condition. If harsh shifting persists after software update, the valve body may need replacement ($800-1,500). Full transmission fluid change (not flush) every 30,000 miles with Hyundai SP-IV-RR fluid.
symptoms: Harsh jolt on 1-2 upshift
Delay when pressing gas to pass
Clunk shifting from park to drive
Hunting between gears on hills
Transmission hesitation at low speed

citations.title: Hyundai TSB 21-AT-002 - Shift Quality Improvement
PalisadeForum.com - Transmission Shift Quality Thread

communityRecommendations.content: Use only Hyundai SP-IV-RR ATF for fluid changes - incompatible fluid causes shift issues
After a TCM update, the transmission needs 500-1,000 miles of driving to fully relearn your driving patterns
